title: Choose the marketing home
question: The roll assigned The cull list. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Brand stays fixed: Ink, Paper, Gate Orange, Inter, stencil 2.

options.label: The cull list
options.thesis: The home is a REST catalog being crossed out until a handful of named tools remain.
options.viewport: A long inventory fills the first screen; struck rows recede; six kept tools sit in full Ink; Sign up sits in the margin of the cut.
options.risk: Reads as documentation, not a product you can start today, if Sign up is not at the cut.

raised.raise: The row under decision is the only full-ink row; already-cut rows thin to gray.
Kept tools stack as solid Ink blocks; cut endpoints leave Paper voids.
A single vertical count (50 → n) rules every line of the list.

options.label: The gate cut
options.thesis: The first viewport is the 2 as a cut between a wide REST catalog and the small tool set that passed.
options.viewport: Left: noisy endpoint list. Center: the stencil 2 as the gate. Right: six named tools and Sign up at the opening.
options.risk: The 2 becomes a decorative mascot if the two sides are not real product content.

options.label: The two doors
options.thesis: GUI and Platform MCP open as two equal doors onto the same server.
options.viewport: Two columns from the first fold share one live server in the middle; Sign up is the threshold before either door.
options.risk: Dual authoring can bury the same-day loop if neither door shows server → tool → URL.

options.label: Annotated keep/cut
options.thesis: The catalog is a measured document: every keep or cut has a leader line to the rule that allowed it.
options.viewport: A keep/cut inventory with leader lines to mutation guard, the 50-tool cap, and agent-facing names; Sign up sits at the last kept row.
options.case: Holds clarity — consultants already read annotated specs; loses identification with the source subculture.
options.risk: Callouts can crowd the offer until it reads as a legal sheet.

options.label: Triggered catalog
options.thesis: The first screen is a bench: one catalog, many endpoints, you trigger the handful that lock still.
options.viewport: A measured bench shows endpoints as traces; a trigger locks six named tools; Sign up sits on the bezel, not inside the glass.
options.case: Holds identification as an instrument; loses clarity because a trace does not say REST-to-MCP in one glance.
options.risk: The bench can hide Sign up and the same-day loop behind a demo.

options.label: Live set, not live mark
options.thesis: One control updates the visible live tool set together — never the wordmark.
options.viewport: A single control thins the catalog; the custom wordmark does not redraw.
options.case: Loses both axes: regenerating the mark violates the brand lock, and a parametric toy is not this audience.
options.kept: One control updates the visible live set together.
options.risk: Any live-drawn 2 would break the master wordmark.

options.label: Newest cut is darkest
options.thesis: Fluid ornament hid the offer; only the ink hierarchy was kept.
options.case: Loses identification and clarity: marbling conceals REST-to-MCP.
options.kept: The row under decision is the only full-ink row.
options.risk: A decorative surface would hide Sign up.

options.label: Blocks and voids
options.thesis: Surreal weather architecture hid the job.
options.case: Loses both axes: consultants do not identify with a cloud quarry.
options.kept: Kept tools as solid blocks; cut endpoints leave voids.
options.risk: Fantasy architecture cannot prove a hosted gateway.

options.label: Count axis
options.thesis: A vertical ocean metaphor hid the product.
options.viewport: Not shown as a dive wall.
options.case: Loses both axes: a descent does not make signup obvious.
options.kept: A single vertical count (50 → n) rules the list.
